verified: Stats Perform's Opta is a structured football event-data provider (branded "celebrating 30 years in 2026," with continuous data since 1996). Official pages publicly verify: 7.2+ PB of proprietary data across 3,900+ competitions and 20+ sports; data "dating back to the 1800s" for some sports; collection via expert human analysts at Opta Centres of Excellence plus optical tracking and proprietary AI models, governed by standardized "Opta Event Definitions." The Opta Data Feeds page explicitly lists match data including team info, players (starting lineups, substitutions), referees (names), and events (goals, cards), with "location coordinates for every on-ball event." The Opta Event Definitions page defines shot types (on/off target, blocked), shot origin (ball position when shot taken), expected goals (xG) and its variables (assist type, shot angle, distance, header, big chance), and three card classes (yellow, 2nd yellow, red). The APIs & Data Delivery FAQ verifies RESTful APIs, websockets, push/pull feeds and S3 delivery in JSON/XML with "sub-second latency," and unique game/team/player IDs. Opta Vision adds XY tracking for all 22 players (2M+ points/game) across 80+ competitions, synchronized to events. Historical product material (Opta Analyst atlas) states World Cup data back to 1930 and granular World Cup team/player data back to 1966; Opta Vision historical World Cup data for 2010-2022. In Jan 2026 FIFA named Stats Perform its first official worldwide betting-data/streaming distributor with exclusive World Cup 2026 (48 teams/104 matches) rights through 2029. Pricing is NOT public: "products and pricing are tailored," custom quote via sales only; custom licensing available "by competition, country, or data level." Licensing is via a Master License Agreement + Work Orders; the MLA prohibits sublicensing/redistribution and building archival files without consent, but those clauses are framed around Licensed Materials/AP/Getty media and Work Order scope. No official source verifies a research-vs-commercial distinction, AI/model-training terms, specific live latency for event feeds, event-correction protocols, or a self-serve historical export — all require vendor confirmation.

provider: StatsBomb (Hudl) — commercial football event data (StatsBomb Services Ltd, a Hudl company). Products: Event Data, 360 Data, and the Live (Live Analysis Platform) Data API; plus a separate free "Public/Open Data" research dataset.
verified: From official sources, StatsBomb (now part of Hudl) sells structured football event data described as "over 3,400 events per match" across "190+ competitions," with player-location/360 data bundled "for 40+ key leagues" at no extra cost; the recruitment/analysis platform cites "170+ leagues" and "160+ insight metrics." StatsBomb publishes a detailed event specification (Open Data Events v4.0.0, "last updated 08 May 2019") that documents the schema shared by its data: millisecond timestamps (timestamp, minute, second, period, index), a full enumerated event-type list (Pass, Shot, Dribble, Substitution, Bad Behaviour, Foul Committed, Goal Keeper, Injury Stoppage, Referee Ball-Drop, Starting XI, Tactical Shift, etc.), shots with statsbomb_xg, end_location (x,y,z), freeze_frame (positions of relevant players), technique/body_part/type/outcome; stable integer player IDs (player.id) and team IDs; a 25-entry tactical position guide (position id/name); card classes via the "card" attribute (Yellow Card / Second Yellow / Red Card) on Bad Behaviour and Foul Committed; substitutions with replacement player and outcome (Injury / Tactical); lineups/benches via Starting XI/Tactical Shift tactics+lineup objects and jersey_number. The Live Analysis Platform API (GraphQL at https://live-api.statsbomb.com/v1/graphql) supports near-realtime subscriptions and historical queries for licensed competitions, with event status (events published before fully formed; status set to COMPLETE when all data present), updated_at ordering, and explicit notes that xG values and rarer corrections may update during/soon after a match. StatsBomb has officially released free event (and some 360) datasets for the World Cup, Euros (Euro 2024 incl. 360), Copa América 2024, and AFCON 2023. The free Public/Open Data is governed by the "StatsBomb Public Data User Agreement" (last updated 8 Sep 2023), which restricts it to research/analysis and explicitly forbids commercial exploitation, redistribution/resale, and reverse engineering, requires StatsBomb attribution + logo, and states all data remains StatsBomb's property. Commercial pricing and commercial-license terms are NOT published; access is via a sales/demo contact form and Customer Success-issued credentials (Client_ID/Client_Secret; tokens expire after 24h).

fields.event_types: Verifiable. Spec enumerates a full event-type list with IDs, including Pass(30), Shot(16), Dribble(14), Carry(43), Ball Receipt(42), Pressure(17), Duel(4), Tackle (Duel/Tackle), Interception(10), Block(6), Clearance(9), Foul Won(21), Foul Committed(22), Bad Behaviour(24), Goal Keeper(23), Substitution(19), Player On(26)/Player Off(27), Own Goal For/Against, Injury Stoppage(40), Referee Ball-Drop(41), Error(37), Miscontrol(38), Offside(8), 50/50(33), Starting XI(35), Tactical Shift(36), Half Start(18)/Half End(34). fields.shot_locations: Verifiable. Shots carry pitch 'location' (x,y) and 'end_location' as (x,y) or (x,y,z) using documented pitch coords (120x80) and goal coords with z (e.g., shot impact height); 'Shot Fidelity Version 2' uses high-fidelity x,y coordinates for shots and freeze frames.
fields.xg: Verifiable. Spec defines 'statsbomb_xg' = 'The StatsBomb expected goals value calculated for the shot' (numeric, e.g., 0.15). Live API exposes an 'xg' field on shot events (may populate/update after the event is first published). Marketed as 'The Most Accurate Expected Goals (xG) Model in Football' using shot impact height and goalkeeper/defender locations.
fields.lineups: Verifiable. Starting XI event (id 35) 'Indicates the players in the starting 11, their position and the team's formation' via tactics(formation)+lineup objects; separate Open Data 'Lineups' files (Open Data Lineups v2.0.0) exist; Live API exposes live_lineup queries. Tactics lineup object includes jersey_number, player(id/name), position(id/name).
fields.benches: unknown_requires_vendor_confirmation. Starting XI and Lineups objects document the players in the XI and lineup, but a distinct, explicitly labeled 'bench/substitutes list' field is not documented in the public Events spec consulted (substitutes are observable when they enter via Substitution/Player On events). Full bench roster representation in the commercial feed requires vendor confirmation.
fields.substitutions: Verifiable. Substitution event (id 19) with 'replacement' (player coming on; main event player = player going off) and outcome attribute 102/'Injury' or 103/'Tactical'. Also Player Off(27)/Player On(26) events, with Player Off 'Permanent' flag for no-subs-left injury scenarios.
fields.player_ids: Verifiable. Each event carries player as object with integer 'id' and 'name' (e.g., 5079 / 'Zlatan Ibrahimovic'); recipients, replacements, and freeze-frame players also carry player id/name. IDs are stable identifiers in the StatsBomb schema; Live API exposes player_id. (Cross-provider mapping not addressed.)
fields.positions: Verifiable. 'position' object (id/name) on events plus a 25-entry Tactical Positions Guide (1 GK ... 23 ST, 24 LCF, 25 SS) in Appendix 1; positions also appear in Starting XI/Tactical Shift lineups and shot freeze frames.
fields.cards: Verifiable. Card classes are enumerated as a 'card' attribute: on Bad Behaviour event (65/Yellow Card, 66/Second Yellow, 67/Red Card) and on Foul Committed (5/Yellow Card, 6/Second Yellow, 7/Red Card). Live API exposes a generic 'card: String' field (subtypes per the event spec).
fields.injuries: Partially verifiable. The schema captures in-match injury signals: 'Injury Stoppage' event (id 40, with in_chain), 'Referee Ball-Drop' (id 41), substitution outcome 'Injury' (102), Player Off 'Permanent' (no subs left due to injury), and pass outcome 'Injury Clearance' (74). A separate structured player-injury/availability dataset (status, expected return) is NOT documented = unknown_requires_vendor_confirmation.
fields.referee: Partially verifiable. The event schema models referee-driven actions (Half Start/End as referee whistle, Referee Ball-Drop, Foul Committed/Won with advantage/penalty/card). fields.live_feed: Verifiable. Live Analysis Platform Data API (GraphQL, https://live-api.statsbomb.com/v1/graphql) provides 'near-realtime' subscriptions to events and player/team stats for matches currently being played, plus queries for active or licensed historical matches; events may be published before fully formed and status set to 'COMPLETE' once all accompanying data is present.

verified: Sportmonks publicly documents a REST "Football API" (v3) covering 2,300-2,500+ leagues including the World Cup, UEFA Euro, Copa America, AFCON, and the major domestic leagues, with a documented entity/include model. Officially verifiable: the Fixtures endpoint exposes events, lineups, formations, statistics, scores, periods, referees, ballCoordinates, predictions, and odds via includes. Match events are a documented taxonomy with codes (GOAL, OWNGOAL, PENALTY, MISSED_PENALTY, penalty-shootout, YELLOWCARD, REDCARD, YELLOWREDCARD, SUBSTITUTION, and VAR/goal-review events) carrying player_id, related_player_id, minute, extra_minute, result, info, and sort_order (docs instruct sorting by sort_order, not minute, which captures VAR/correction chains at the data level). Shot statistics are aggregate counts (total, on/off target, inside/outside box, blocked) with NO shot-location or shot-coordinate fields documented; xG is offered as paid add-ons (xG Basic post-match / xG Advanced live) and is AGGREGATED per team and per player only — docs explicitly state no per-chance/per-shot xG. Lineups distinguish starters (type_id 11) from bench (type_id 12) with player_id, jersey_number, formation_field, position and detailedPosition includes; substitutions are tracked via the Events include. Livescores update on a documented ~10-second cycle with a stated <15-second real-time latency claim on the product page. Historical data uses the same fixtures endpoints with date-range queries (max 100-day window/request); seasons older than a standard ~3-season window require a one-time Historical add-on (Enterprise includes full history). Published plan pricing: Starter EUR29, Growth EUR99, Pro EUR249/mo, Enterprise custom, plus add-ons (xG, odds, historical, news, transfers, extra leagues/calls). Rights: distribution/storage of data is permitted, reselling the raw product is forbidden without consent, and logos/photos require the user to arrange IP rights. A 14-day free trial and a permanent free plan (Danish Superliga + Scottish Premiership) exist; Enterprise/quotes go through Contact & Support / support@sportmonks.com.

provider: API-Football / API-Sports (api-football.com / api-sports.io). REST JSON football data API; current version v3. Self-serve dashboard product with a permanent free tier and prepaid paid plans; also distributed via RapidAPI. Owned/operated by API-Sports.
verified: From official API-Football/API-Sports pages (documentation-v3, pricing, coverage, terms of service, and official news/endpoint posts), the following is publicly verifiable. The API is organized around a fixture ID; /fixtures returns referee, venue, status, score and can embed events, lineups, statistics and players. Each league-season carries a coverage object of boolean flags (events, lineups, statistics_fixtures, statistics_players, standings, players, top_scorers, top_assists, top_cards, injuries, predictions, odds) declaring what is collected; flags are aspirational, not a per-match guarantee. The /leagues catalog spans 1,200+ competitions including leagues, cups, qualifiers and friendlies, with a per-competition seasons array; FIFA World Cup 2026 is league=1, season=2026 with fixtures/events/lineups/statistics/players/standings/predictions/odds/injuries declared. Events carry type (Goal, Card, subst, Var) plus a detail field and time.elapsed/time.extra; VAR events exist from 2020-21. Lineups expose formation, startXI, substitutes (bench), coach, player number, position (pos) and grid coordinates. Stable numeric IDs exist for players, teams, leagues and fixtures. Injuries endpoint gives type (Injury/Suspension) and reason. Live data uses fixtures?live=all and is described as updated roughly every 15 seconds, with the provider explicitly warning there may be a delay between reality and availability. The Terms state data is provided 'as is' with no guarantee, may contain errors, errors are reported via the support tool, incorrect/missing data is not grounds for refund, and update frequencies are indicative only. Pricing is public: Free 100 req/day, Pro USD 19/mo 7,500 req/day, Mega USD 39/mo 150,000 req/day, custom up to ~1.5M/day via dashboard chat. Crucially, the Terms state API-Football grants no publication license and no commercial rights over the competitions; users must obtain any needed rights from competent authorities/rights holders; reselling/redistributing the data to third parties is prohibited.

provider: Sportradar (Sportradar AG) — Soccer API and Soccer Extended API (Media/Data Content division), documented at developer.sportradar.com
verified: From Sportradar's official developer portal and corporate site it is publicly verifiable that Sportradar offers a Soccer API and a Soccer Extended API delivering structured football-event data for 650+ competitions across a global suite of men's and women's leagues, with coverage organized into 9 tiers (Tier 1 most comprehensive, Tier 9 post-match results only). Official coverage documentation and the public Coverage Matrix confirm coverage of men's senior international and continental tournaments (World Championship/World Cup, European Championship, Copa America, Africa Cup of Nations) at competition-dependent tiers. Historical data is documented as available back to 2007 for some competitions (depending on tier/coverage), while a standard subscription returns the current season plus two previous seasons; 17 historical feeds and on-demand match replay (Simulations) are documented. The Sport Event Timeline / Sport Event Summary schemas publicly document: a 43-event-type timeline; x/y event coordinates on a 0-100 pitch; shots with on/off-target, blocked, body-part and zone/location splits; expected goals via goals_expected and goals_expected_created (player and team); pre/post lineups with formations, benches, substitutions (substituted_in/out); stable player IDs; positions (GK/DEF/MID/FWD plus tactical roles); three card classes (yellow_card, red_card, yellow_red_card); injury/availability via the Missing Players endpoint (injury, illness, suspension, other); and referee officials with stable referee IDs and official-type roles (main_referee, VAR, assistants). Live delivery uses HTTP-chunked push (5-second heartbeat) on Realtime plans and REST live endpoints with a documented 1-second TTL / realtime updates; corrections are exposed via Sport Events Updated (last 24h) and Sport Events Removed (2-week retention) feeds. Commercially it is a paid B2B license (not callable from client apps); a 30-day free trial is advertised but is restricted to internal, non-commercial evaluation; pricing is by custom quote (no public rate card); and the terms explicitly prohibit using Sportradar's AI models/algorithms/outputs/IP to train any AI/ML models, prohibit resale/sublicensing/derivative works, and require destruction of historical/non-realtime data on termination.

Live coverage is tier-dependent. Source: soccer-ig-push, soccer-ig-live-match-retrieval.
fields.latency: No single published end-to-end latency SLA (in seconds) is publicly documented. Documented timing: push heartbeat every 5 seconds; live REST endpoints have a 1-second TTL/cache with 'Realtime' updates and may be polled as fast as every 1 second when a match is live. Actual delivery latency / SLA = unknown_requires_vendor_confirmation. Source: soccer-ig-push, soccer-ig-update-frequencies, soccer-live-timelines.
fields.corrections: Yes. 'Sport Events Updated' feed returns IDs of events modified in the last 24 hours (captures stat revisions/event corrections); 'Sport Events Removed' returns IDs of events removed due to entry errors, remaining in the feed for 2 weeks. Source: soccer-ig-api-basics / FAQ.
fields.historical_export_api: Yes (API access; no documented one-shot bulk download). Historical seasons are queried through the standard REST feeds (17 historical endpoints) by competition_id/season_id/player_id, with no separate package required for documented depth; on-demand replay of recorded matches (REST and Push) is provided via 'Simulations'. Bulk historical export/dump terms not publicly specified — confirm with vendor. Source: soccer-ig-historical-data, soccer-ig-api-basics.

rights.licensing_model: Paid B2B commercial license under Sportradar Terms & Conditions plus per-product Order Forms; APIs are explicitly B2B and 'not intended to be called directly from a client application.' A 30-day free trial is advertised (no purchase necessary) but is for internal testing/evaluation and non-commercial use only — data may not be published/displayed commercially during the trial. Source: get-started, authentication, sports-data-api product page, terms-and-conditions.
rights.research_use: Not offered as a distinct discounted 'research/academic' license in the public terms. The free trial permits internal, non-commercial testing/evaluation only (no commercial publication/display). Any academic/research production use would fall under a standard paid license — unknown_requires_vendor_confirmation for special research terms. Source: terms-and-conditions (Free Trial clause).
rights.commercial_use: Permitted under a paid license for display on designated Properties (non-exclusive, worldwide, revocable; perpetual only for archiving). Gambling/betting-related use and advertising-associated use require express prior written approval. Source: terms-and-conditions.
rights.storage_restrictions: Customers must use encryption/secure technologies for processing/transfer/storage (incl. backups). On termination, must cease use and destroy all historical/non-realtime data and databases (and certify destruction if requested); in-progress seasonal data may be retained for original contracted purposes under the archival license. Source: terms-and-conditions, media-data-addendum.
rights.model_training: Explicitly prohibited: customer 'shall not use Sportradar's AI models, algorithms, Outputs or other intellectual property to develop or train any artificial intelligence, machine learning algorithms or models.' Sportradar retains the right to use Data to improve/benchmark/develop its own products and owns IP developed using Data. (Whether using the underlying event DATA — vs. Sportradar's models/outputs — to train models is permitted is not unambiguous and requires vendor confirmation.) Source: terms-and-conditions.
rights.redistribution: Prohibited without written agreement: no resale, sub-licensing, distribution to affiliates/third parties, no service-bureau/time-sharing use, and no copying/modifying/derivative works of the Company Materials. Source: terms-and-conditions, media-data-addendum.
rights.public_price: No public price / rate card. Pricing is by custom quote via Order Forms; the product page states two package types (Real-time vs Standard, differentiated by request limits) but directs users to 'get in touch for a custom quote.' Source: sports-data-api product page, terms-and-conditions.

procurement: Official self-service trial and quote process: (1) Sign up for a 30-day free trial at the Sportradar developer console (console.sportradar.com) / marketplace (marketplace.sportradar.com) — 'No purchase necessary,' internal/non-commercial evaluation only; an account yields a 40-character master API key usable across products. (2) Review docs and test in the sandbox at developer.sportradar.com (Soccer API / Soccer Extended). (3) For production/commercial access, pricing, and Realtime/push plans, contact Sportradar sales via the contact form on sportradar.com ('get in touch for a custom quote'); Realtime/push trial access is requested separately through a sales representative. Pricing and contract terms are set in individual Order Forms. (Per the task constraints I did not sign up, log in, submit forms, or call any API — this reflects the publicly documented process only.)
uncertainties: latency: no published end-to-end/SLA latency figure in seconds (only 5s push heartbeat and 1s live TTL are documented) — actual delivery latency requires vendor confirmation
